title: More Than Conquerors
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Christians should have an otherworldly confidence. God gave his own Son for us, so who can condemn us, and what can separate us from his love?
exhortation: In light of this passage, it struck me that Christians ought to have a little bit of crazy in them: a strangeness, an otherworldly flavor that some might even take as a little nuts.

I love reading about missionaries. One of my favorites is John Paton. When he talked about going to islands of cannibals to preach the gospel, people told him he was a little nuts. But a true-blooded Christian only seems that way because he has a confidence that is so sure. It's like facing off against the greatest athlete ever to play his sport: for him, winning isn't even a question. He doesn't fear the competition, the pain or the cost. The win is a foregone conclusion.

How can you have that kind of confidence? Because God has called you his son or his daughter. Because he already gave the most he possibly could, his own Son, for your sake, to cancel a debt you could never pay. So who could possibly condemn us? If Christ conquered every enemy, even death itself, what charge could anyone bring against me? And what circumstance could tear me from a love that has already gone to the furthest possible length? Not a lost job, not the most gut-wrenching, unexpected death, not disease, not even persecution. Nothing can shake our confidence, because nothing defeats the love of God in Christ Jesus.

Why should we have an otherworldly confidence? Because we're playing this game of life with house money. We can't be touched. We belong to another world. So don't be deceived by the enemy today. Don't let him bring up the sins of your past, even your recent past, and use them to put a wall between you and the love of God, because they can't. Your confidence today is in Christ and what he has done for you. That confidence and joy are yours in Jesus Christ. Live in them.
prayer: Lord, what love is this, deeper than the sea, higher than the mountains of our sin, deeper than the depths of our depravity. You have saved us. Your love is stronger. Help us walk in that truth today. When the enemy brings up our sin, help us say, "And what of it? My Savior has paid for that." All the sins of our past and all the sins to come: Jesus will bring us through to our glorious future.

Brothers and sisters, we believe this. It is true, and we see it in God's word. Hold fast to this truth this morning and throughout your day. And don't forget to be grateful and tell Jesus how wonderful he is and how grateful we are for what he has done for us. In Jesus' name.
